"Create a first-person 3D exploration game with a visual style similar to Counter-Strike: realistic textures, dim lighting, industrial/village environment, FPS camera. The player controls a healer named Zhanat Kozhamzharov and can walk around with WASD. NPCs stand in the world and show a floating request icon above their heads (e.g., \"My back hurts,\" \"I feel sick,\" \"I am stressed\").

When the player looks at an NPC and presses E, a healing sequence starts:
1. The player character raises a glowing red-hot sword to his mouth and touches the tip of the sword to his tongue.
2. He takes a sip of water from a bottle (a simple drinking animation).
3. He sprays the water through his mouth over the red-hot sword tip, creating a burst of steam and bubble particles (use particle effects: white steam clouds and small bubbles).
4. The steam cloud floats toward the NPC and envelops them.
5. The NPC's request icon disappears, and they play a short \"relieved\" animation (e.g., relaxed posture) with a gratitude line.

Game rules: no combat, no weapons used against people, no fail state. The goal is to heal every NPC in the level. Include a HUD counter \"People healed: X/Y\". Use warm orange and red lighting for the steam effect. Playable in landscape on mobile. Keep the code simple and modular so I can later add more NPCs and dialogue lines.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

  open [url]                  open the browser

  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable first-person 3D healing exploration game set in a dim industrial village.
- Let players heal every NPC through a gentle sword-and-water ritual, with no combat or fail state.

## Requirements
- WASD movement, first-person camera, look-at targeting and E interaction.
- NPC request icons, healing sequence with glowing sword, drinking, steam and bubbles, followed by gratitude and a relieved animation.
- HUD counter for people healed; warm orange/red healing effects; playable on landscape mobile.
- Keep the code simple and modular for adding NPCs and dialogue.

## Decisions
- Built as a standalone Three.js scene in a single HTML file.
- Assumed five villagers and added the stated healer name, Zhanat Kozhamzharov.
- Chose a twilight village courtyard with workshop details and original procedural materials.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added village scene, five modular NPC requests, first-person movement and camera controls, healing interaction/effects, HUD, and touch controls in `index.html`.
- Added opening and completion screens, in-game messages, and restart flow.
- JavaScript module passed `node --check`.
- Started a local HTTP server and opened the game in Playwright; saved and inspected `screenshots/village.jpg` and `screenshots/playing.jpg`.

### Active
- No active changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally recheck the latest `index.html` in-browser after the final changes to the first-person props and favicon.
2. Summarize the finished work and note that visual verification was performed.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/playing.jpg`: Captured in-game view.
- `screenshots/village.jpg`: Captured opening screen.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The Playwright check showed one console error from a missing `/favicon.ico`; a data-URI favicon was added afterward, but not rechecked.
- The app uses Three.js from the jsDelivr CDN.
